title: Living-off-the-land espionage: mshta -> certutil/regsvr32 -> WMI persistence + lateral, slow exfil (Windows)

alert.summary: Threat-hunt alert: regsvr32.exe making periodic large-upload HTTPS connections to an external host, with no corresponding browser activity, on RND-WS-11.

decoy_hypothesis.statement: H1: The alert is external brute-force reconnaissance from {bf_ip} against the local Administrator - an internet attacker is forcing their way in, and the IT helpdesk PsExec activity is the resulting hands-on-keyboard movement.

corrected_hypothesis.statement: H2: The intrusion is a living-off-the-land espionage actor on RND-WS-11. A malicious HTA (mshta) launched from Outlook used certutil to download+decode a payload and regsvr32 (squiblydoo) to execute it, established WMI event-subscription persistence, used wmic /node to move to RND-FS-03, and beacons low-and-slow to a known-bad host with periodic large uploads (data exfil). The internet brute-force is benign scanner noise and the helpdesk PsExec gpupdate is sanctioned admin tooling.
corrected_hypothesis.rationale_suffix: All malicious execution chains from mshta->certutil->regsvr32 under s.kapoor with WMI persistence and exfil to a malicious host; the brute-force never succeeded and the helpdesk host is in the sanctioned asset inventory.

refutation.no_success_reason: every logon from {bf_ip} is a 4625 failure - the external scanner never authenticated

containment: Isolate RND-WS-11 and triage RND-FS-03 for the wmic-delivered payload.
Block egress to 203.0.113.88 / cdn-telemetry-sync.example.net at the edge firewall.
Remove the WMI __FilterToConsumerBinding 'WinSyncTrigger' and the winsync.dll payload.
Hunt fleet-wide for mshta launched by Office and regsvr32 /i:scrobj.dll (squiblydoo).
Reset s.kapoor credentials; review what regsvr32 uploaded (assume R&D data exfiltrated).
Baseline WMI permanent event subscriptions and restrict wmic /node between workstations.
